speak verb

also speak Latin, do you speak Latin?, know a language, do you know Latin?, do you understand Latin?, are you learning Latin?, speak Latin fluently

M-O s.v. speak: do you speak Latin?
Traupman 337

Latīnē loquī

speak Latin (Graecē loquī, speak Greek)

The adverb names the language; for modern ones see in English, in Bulgarian, in Portuguese. Lewis & Short notes that Latīnē loquī can also mean to speak good, plain Latin (Cic. Brut. 166).

Other words

  • Latīnē scīre — know Latin

    also used · classical · Cic. Brut. 140: nōn enim tam praeclārum est scīre Latīnē quam turpe nescīre; Cic. Caecin. 55 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 30: Scīsne Latīnē loquī?; Traupman 337

    Its opposite is Latīnē nescīre.

Examples

  • nōn tamen hoc adeō superstitiōsē fierī velim, ut diū tantum Graecē loquātur aut discat, sīcut plērīsque mōris est

    But I would not have this done so rigidly that he speaks or learns only Greek for a long time, as most people do.Quint. 1.1.13

  • nōn enim tam praeclārum est scīre Latīnē quam turpe nescīre

    For knowing Latin is not so much a credit as not knowing it is a disgrace.Cic. Brut. 140

  • scīs enim mē Graecē loquī in Latīnō sermōne nōn plūs solēre quam in Graecō Latīnē

    For you know I am no more in the habit of speaking Greek in a Latin conversation than Latin in a Greek one.Cic. Tusc. 1.15
